circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, and has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that serves as the venue for the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix, along with supporting motorsport events including the Supercars Championship Melbourne SuperSprint. The circuit holds an FIA Grade 1 classification, meeting the highest international safety and facility standards.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a redesign and renaming in the 1990s, the track resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital positioned along Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted the 2016 European Grand Prix before establishing itself as the home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onward.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the region's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix, marking the sport's first Middle Eastern race. Beyond F1, the venue accommodates various racing formats including GP2 competition, 24-hour endurance events, and briefly hosted Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 until 2010, while maintaining FIA Grade 1 certification with multiple configurable track layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing disciplines. The venue accommodates over 140,000 spectators and holds the highest FIA safety classification.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located near the town of Spa in Belgium's Wallonia region, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a Formula One staple since 1950, when it hosted a race during the championship's inaugural season. The venue has held the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only brief interruptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre street circuit that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its Formula One commitments, the track has accommodated various international motorsport competitions including sports car racing series and North American racing championships.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is renowned as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place annually between 2004 and 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix, which commenced in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone has been England's premier motor racing venue since hosting the inaugural British Grand Prix in 1948. The circuit gained further significance by staging the opening round of the first-ever Formula One World Championship season in 1950, and after alternating with other tracks through the 1950s and 1980s, it became the permanent home of Britain's grand prix from 1987 onward.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One race held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue, the track was constructed outside Budapest near a highway after initial plans for a street circuit in the city's main park were abandoned.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza, located near Milan in northern Italy, is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, the venue earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" from its extended straights and fast-paced corner design that characterizes high-velocity motorsport.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track hosts major international racing events, particularly Formula One and Super Formula championships, and accommodates up to 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that weaves through Paradise, Nevada, utilizing the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The 3. 8-mile layout passes several iconic venues including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique Grand Prix venue that combines high-speed racing with the city's most recognizable entertainment destinations.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304 km Mexico City circuit is named after two fatal racing drivers, the Rodríguez brothers, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current layout, following a gap since 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: Miami's street circuit weaves around Hard Rock Stadium, measuring 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and supporting average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Built specifically for Formula One by specialist designers, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022 as the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, circling the harbour in the Principality of Monaco. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known as Monte Carlo due to its location predominantly within that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km Dutch motorsport facility that welcomed Formula One's return in 2021 with the reinstatement of the Dutch Grand Prix. The track will host the grand prix through 2026 under its current sponsorship agreement.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, spans 5. 419 kilometers and features a 1. 068-kilometer main straight, holding an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace. The venue hosts major motorsport events and features additional facilities including a karting track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street course situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021. The venue also began accommodating Formula E racing in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue located in Singapore that winds around the Marina Bay area, spanning across the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations that test all aspects of vehicle performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates nearly 141,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts numerous international racing events including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and endurance racing competitions, having previously accommodated various other motorsport series ranging from IndyCar to rallycross.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a British-Thai racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand in international motorsport competition.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships during his 23-season career, accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours wins and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both the Formula One World Championship and the World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes' Formula One lineup in 2025 and has already secured six race victories in the championship.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: British driver Oliver Bearman currently races for Haas in Formula One, bringing his talents to the American team's competitive efforts.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One for Audi, bringing his motorsport expertise to the team's grid lineup.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. He has achieved two runner-up finishes in the championship during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, and has secured 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his 13-season career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor who currently drives for Alpine in Formula One racing.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while competing in European Le Mans Series prototype racing. He has participated in seven Grand Prix events spanning the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. He achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri earlier in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French banner.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari who has secured seven World Drivers' Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple performance records in the sport, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One while maintaining an impressive endurance racing résumé that includes a 2015 Le Mans 24 Hours victory with Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who has competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he races in the World Endurance Championship for BMW with WRT and participates part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series driving for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver who clinched the 2025 world championship while racing for McLaren. The accomplished driver has secured 12 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Haas. The versatile racer previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio "Checo" Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that has yielded six Grand Prix victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver for McLaren, has secured nine Formula One victories throughout his four-year tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who competed in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his 14-season career. He claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver, competes for Mercedes in Formula One and has secured seven race victories since entering the sport eight seasons ago.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. He previously competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to sports car racing, including prior experience in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One, where he races for the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, has held reserve positions with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls during his time in Formula One between 2021 and 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has been a dominant force in Formula One, claiming four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories, establishing himself as one of the sport's most successful competitors.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver who holds the distinction of being the sole driver from China to have competed in Formula One. He raced in the championship between 2022 and 2024, and currently serves in a reserve capacity for the Cadillac team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, following its rebranding from Renault F1 Team to promote the French automaker's sports car division while serving as Renault's official works squad until the manufacturer's 2025 departure. Operating under a French licence with Mercedes power units, Alpine achieved its only victory during this era through Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has entered Formula One multiple times throughout its history, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team designation.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Ferrari's Formula One operation, known as Scuderia Ferrari HP, represents the racing division of the Italian luxury automaker and stands as the sport's longest-established and most accomplished team. Since entering the World Championship in 1950, the squad has maintained continuous participation throughout the competition's entire history, earning recognition through the iconic symbol associated with their brand identity.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas, the NASCAR team owner, founded this American-licensed Formula One outfit in 2014, launching its competitive program in 2016. The organization has recently undergone leadership changes, with Ayao Komatsu assuming the principal role following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: The Swiss-based Sauber team, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, progressed from sports car construction to become an independent Formula One constructor after debuting in 1993, with notable early success including a 1989 Le Mans victory alongside Mercedes-Benz. Following numerous transformations across three decades, the operation ceased competing in 2025 as racing history's fourth-longest-running constructor, having been purchased by Audi in 2024 to serve as the foundational platform for Audi's factory F1 entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technology facility in Woking, operating as a subsidiary within the wider McLaren Group corporate structure. The team competes under commercial sponsorship partnerships while remaining part of a larger automotive and motorsport conglomerate.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One continuously since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current iteration based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The team, officially Mercedes-AMG Petronas, restructured its ownership in 2022 to include equal stakes from Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. Mercedes-branded entries are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" throughout their racing history.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that debuted in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned outfits in the sport. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull's second constructor alongside Red Bull Racing.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as Red Bull's second team. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the squad operates alongside Red Bull Racing under the ownership of Austrian conglomerate Red Bull GmbH.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing competes in Formula One under an Austrian licence while operating from England as part of Red Bull GmbH's motorsport portfolio. Founded in 2005, the team was led by Christian Horner for two decades until Laurent Mekies assumed the role in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, represents a continuation of Williams's racing ambitions following his earlier unsuccessful F1 venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team will compete in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and remains one of the sport's established operations.
